title: The front-matter codec is line-oriented: collections must stay inline
body: parse_front_matter iterates block.split("\n") and matches one key per line, so any YAML block sequence or nested mapping breaks parsing outright. OKF typed links are written as inline flow mappings ([{target: "slug", rel: "relates-to"}]) for exactly this reason — valid YAML that an external reader parses and this codec can still own. Adding a structured field? Keep it on one line.

title: Don't hand-build page front matter in eval fixtures
body: eval/corpus.py, eval/realistic.py, and eval/selection.py each kept their own copy of the front-matter dict and all three silently went stale when the page format changed. Build a WikiNode and call wiki_store.node_front_matter(node) instead — one mapping, one place to update.

title: Adopting an external format means taking its semantics, not just its names
body: OKF v0.2 rewrites `timestamp` on every edit, so mapping Memex's immutable `created` onto it would have let any OKF tool destroy the creation date. Before renaming a field to match an external spec, read that spec's writer to see when it mutates the field — the name is the cheap half of conformance.
